title: 1. Great Wall of China (China)
p1: Length: ~21,196 km (longest wall in the world).
p2: Built to protect China from Mongol invasions.
p3: Took around 2,000 years to complete (7th century BC → 17th century AD).
p4: Made of stone, brick, wood, and earth.
p5: Popular myth: visible from space (not true with the naked eye).

title: 2. Petra (Jordan)
p1: Known as the “Rose City” for its pink sandstone cliffs.
p3: Famous site: Al-Khazneh (The Treasury), carved into rock.
p4: Advanced water system engineering in the desert.
p5: Rediscovered in 1812 by Swiss explorer Johann Burckhardt.

title: 3. Christ the Redeemer (Brazil)
p1: Height: 30 m (98 ft), arm span: 28 m.
p2: Built between 1922–1931 in Rio de Janeiro, on Corcovado Mountain.
p4: Gets struck by lightning often; repairs are common.
p5: Symbol of Christianity, peace, and Brazilian culture.

title: 4. Machu Picchu (Peru)
p1: Built by the Inca civilization in the 15th century.
p2: Located in the Andes Mountains (2,430 m above sea level).
p4: Stones are perfectly cut without cement, making it earthquake-proof.
p5: Remained hidden during the Spanish conquest, so it’s well preserved.

title: 5. Chichen Itza (Mexico)
p2: Famous pyramid: El Castillo (Temple of Kukulcán) with 365 steps = days in a year.
p3: During equinox, the shadow forms a serpent crawling down the pyramid.
p4: Shows the Mayans’ advanced knowledge of astronomy and mathematics.
p5: Symbolizing the Mayan feathered serpent god, Kukulcán..

title: 6. Roman Colosseum (Italy)
p3: Used for gladiator battles, animal hunts, and dramas.
p4: Made with stone + concrete (revolutionary at that time).

title: 7. Taj Mahal (India)
p1: Made of white marble + precious stones (jade, sapphire, turquoise, etc.).
p2: Built to protect China from Mongol invasions.
p3: Declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
p4: Changes color with time of day: pink (morning), white (afternoon), golden (night).
p5: Famous as the “symbol of eternal love.”
